notes: Reading of the enable / power-good chain (the exact wiring, from the sheets and nets.json):

U52 (IRF9317 P-FET, sheet 24): source = 12P0V_IN (J29 pin 1), drain = 12P0V. Gate N18990890 is pulled to the source by R275 33k; SW6 pins 2/5 (net N18990875) go to the gate divider through R277 22k, and SW6 pins 1/4 are GND. SW6 on (2-1, 5-4) pulls the gate to about 0.4 x 12P0V_IN and the FET conducts; the default position 2&3, 5&6 leaves the gate at the source (off). D3 (SD2114S040S8R0) is the Schottky from 12P0V to 12P0V_PCIEX16; it is not a reverse-polarity diode.

U53 / U58 (MIC26950, sheets 25/29): EN (pin 24) = VDD5V_5P0V / VDD5V_3P3V through R393 4.7k / R286 10k (R319 4.7k / R394 10k); the schematic note says Ven_Hi = 1.2 V min. VDD5V_x is made from 12P0V by Q3 / Q4 (FCX619) with a 5.6 V zener (D5 / D7 CMDZ5L6), so both bucks enable as soon as 12P0V is present. No PG pin is used.

U59 (MIC23303, 1P8V, sheet 25): EN = 5P0V through R328 4.7k / R331 10k (C545 not loaded). PG pin 3 is the net PG_1P8V, pulled up to 1P8V by R325 6.8k, with R358 22k to GND (R48 to 5P0V and C883 are not loaded).
U56 (MIC23303, 1P1V_LPDDR4, sheet 28): EN pin 4 is the net PG_1P8V. This is the only PG -> EN link on the board (also drawn as ENABLE on the block diagram, sheet 23).
U57 (MIC23303, 1P2V_PHY_VSC_FP6, sheet 28): EN = 5P0V through R362 4.7k / R365 0R / R366 10k (C577 not loaded). It is NOT gated by PG_1P8V (PLAN section 4.2 had this wrong).

U54 (MIC22705, VDD, sheet 27): EN/DLY pin 2 is the net EN_1V; R295 (10k to 5P0V) is not loaded, so EN_1V only has C504 1000 pF to GND and is charged by the part's internal 1 uA source: the delay is 1.24 V x 1000 pF / 1 uA = 1.24 ms after 5P0V passes U54's UVLO. Its PG (pin 5) is pulled up to 5P0V by R296 47.5k and goes nowhere else.
U71 (MIC69502WR, 2P5V, sheet 26): EN = 5P0V through R389 20k / R390 20k with C788 0.1 uF (10k x 0.1 uF = 1 ms RC). No PG pin.
U61 (MIC69502WR, VDDA, sheet 29): EN = 3P3V through R338 4.7k / R339 4.7k with C557 0.33 uF (2.35k x 0.33 uF = 0.78 ms RC). No PG pin. VDDA is sensed after the R337 shunt (R499 0R; R501 not loaded).
U17 (MIC23303, 1P5V_DDR3, sheet 26): EN pulled up to 3P3V by R179 10k. PG pulled up to 1P5V_DDR3 by R178 10k, used nowhere else.
U21 (MIC5166, sheet 26): BIAS = 3P3V, VIN = VDDQ = 1P5V_DDR3. EN = net EN_VTT, only pulled up to 3P3V by R200 10k. PG = net PG_VTT, pulled up to 3P3V by R242 1k; nothing else is on PG_VTT.

So the sequence is mostly set by the input rails: 12P0V -> U53 5P0V and U58 3P3V together (6 ms soft-start) -> from 5P0V: U59 1P8V, U57 1P2V, U71 2P5V, and U54 VDD 1.24 ms after 5P0V passes 2.75 V -> PG_1P8V -> U56 1P1V_LPDDR4; from 3P3V: U61 VDDA, U17 1P5V_DDR3 -> U21 VTT/VREF.

Setpoints are computed from each feedback divider and the datasheet reference (MIC23303 0.62 V, MIC22705 0.7 V, MIC69502 0.5 V, MIC26950 0.8 V), so they differ slightly from the rail names (e.g. 1P1V_LPDDR4 = 0.62 x (1 + 237k/294k) = 1.120 V).
Rail capacitance capUF = the sum of the loaded (non-DNL) capacitors from the rail net to GND in footprints.json; it sets how fast a rail discharges once its regulator stops.
Static loads are ASSUMED typical values (not measured) so that the telemetry and the PAC1934 show plausible currents.
